rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

rules.title: FTC: No Sold or Unavailable Units Used to Draw Traffic
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q10
rules.description: Dealers must not advertise cars that have already been paid for and delivered, or are otherwise unavailable, as a tactic to draw consumers in and steer them to higher-priced options. Whether a recently sold unit is a problem depends on timing and the ad's wording; California's 48-hour withdrawal rule (Veh. Code §11713(c)) is the state safe harbor.
rules.fail_condition: Not reliably website-verifiable in one crawl. Flag when inventory diffs show a sold or delivered unit still live beyond 48 hours, especially a price-leader unit
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/

rules.title: FTC: Representative Photos Only When Truly Representative
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q11
rules.description: A representative (stock) photo is allowed only when the pictured vehicle is the same make, model, condition, and all other material characteristics as the car offered, and a reasonable consumer would understand the image is illustrative. Common and generally acceptable for new and in-transit units. For used and antique vehicles, consumers reasonably expect the photo to show the exact car, so stock or representative photos on used listings are a deception risk.
rules.fail_condition: A used or CPO listing uses a stock or representative photo, or a new-vehicle stock photo shows a different trim, color, or equipment than the unit priced
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/

rules.title: FTC: Every Medium Counts, Including Staff Calls and Texts
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q3
rules.description: Dealer and third-party websites, social media, print, roadside signs, and phone calls and text messages with dealer staff are all subject to the FTC Act. Any price a salesperson or BDC agent states by phone or text must be the truthful, all-in price. ComplyAuto flags calls and texts as a new compliance focus.
rules.fail_condition: Not website-verifiable. Advisory reminder: BDC call scripts, SMS templates, and CRM auto-texts that state a price must use the all-in advertised price
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

rules.title: FTC: Shared Responsibility Across Dealer, Vendors, and OEM
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q12
rules.description: Everyone with control over an ad is responsible for the actual price being the most prominent amount. Dealers must give third parties the actual price, take all steps within their control to make it most prominent, and make sure no one at the store gives contradictory instructions. Third-party advertisers must show it most prominently. OEM policies must not conflict. Dealers remain responsible for every ad under their name, including OEM-originated ads. FTC staff (2026-09-30): where an OEM requirement or a listing-platform limitation blocks a most-prominent actual price or an in-transit label and the dealer cannot resolve it, report the OEM or platform to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov; more than one party can be responsible for the same ad.
rules.fail_condition: Advisory: third-party listings, OEM co-op templates, or agency creative show a different or less prominent price than the dealer's actual price, and there is no written correction request on file
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

rules.title: FTC: No Grace Period, and Competitors Can Report You
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q13, Q14
rules.description: Price transparency under Section 5 is not new and has no compliance window; anyone misleading consumers about price risks FTC action now. The FTC invites the public, including competing dealers, to report violations with ad copies or contracts at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. FTC staff (2026-09-30): scam websites impersonating a dealership go to ReportFraud@ftc.gov with the URL and what was copied (branding, inventory, photos).
rules.fail_condition: Advisory for every report: federal exposure is current, not future-dated, unlike the California CARS Act posture
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

rules.title: FTC: Savings and Discount Claims Scoped and Conditioned Honestly
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q5, Q9; FTC staff remarks 2026-09-30
rules.description: A savings or discount claim must be truthful in the context of the whole ad. 'Save $10,000' may not create the impression that the saving applies across inventory when it applies to one vehicle, model, or trim; conditions such as dealer financing, a trade-in, time limits, or model and trim restrictions must be clearly disclosed. Disclosing a condition does not permit a price available only to qualifying buyers to be the most prominent price (FTC staff, 2026-09-30). California adds Veh. Code §11713.1(i) quantity disclosure for class pricing and bars used-vehicle savings claims against MSRP.
rules.fail_condition: A homepage, specials, or search-results page shows a dollar savings or discount claim with no adjacent scope (which unit, model, trim, or stock number) or with an undisclosed financing or trade-in condition. Judgment and human review; the FTC-SAVINGS-SCOPE check flags the pattern
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

rules.title: FTC: Price CTA Buttons Beside the Price, Never Implying a Lower Price
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q4; FTC staff remarks 2026-09-30
rules.description: Buttons such as 'Get My Price' or 'Call for Price' may appear alongside the advertised price (dealers remain free to negotiate), but the wording and presentation must be truthful: the button may not suggest that clicking or calling produces a lower price when it does not, and it may not obscure or contradict the advertised price (FTC staff, 2026-09-30). This is the federal view only. California bars a CTA that stands in place of the total price (CA-CARS-026, CNCDA FAQ Q6 and Q10), so for California stores the price must be on the page and the button may only sit beside it.
rules.fail_condition: A priced page carries a CTA whose text promises a lower, special, or unlocked price ('Unlock savings', 'Get my lower price', 'Click for e-price', 'See your best price') with no such lower price actually available, or a CTA that hides the displayed price. Human review; the FTC-CTA-LOWER-PRICE check flags the wording
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

rules.title: FTC: 'In Transit' Means Already Shipped; Arrival Dates Must Be Real
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q10; FTC staff remarks 2026-09-30
rules.description: Consumers understand 'in transit' to mean the vehicle is already on its way to the dealership. A unit that has not been built or shipped must be described by its actual status (in production, factory order, build to order), not as in transit. An advertised in-transit unit must be available for purchase on arrival and not allocated to another customer's paid order. The Commission has previously pointed to delivery within one to two business days as acceptable; delays outside the dealer's control are judged case by case (an isolated shipping-damage delay differs from a routine pattern), and any stated arrival date or timeline must reflect what the dealer actually knows (FTC staff, 2026-09-30).
rules.fail_condition: A listing labeled in transit that also describes the unit as in production, not yet built, or a factory order; an in-transit unit with no arrival information or with an arrival date the store cannot support; an in-transit unit already allocated to a paid order
rules.source: FTC staff, Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency: FAQs (September 2026), https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/automobile-industry-pricing-transparency-faqs; ComplyAuto analysis (2026-09-16), https://complyauto.com/ftc-issues-dealer-advertising-faqs/; FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

rules.title: FTC: AI-Generated Ad Copy and Imagery Carry the Same Duties
rules.statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC staff remarks 2026-09-30
rules.description: Using AI to create an advertisement does not change the advertiser's obligations or shift responsibility for misleading content. AI-generated text and visuals must be accurate and not deceptive. Practical step from FTC staff (2026-09-30): review AI-generated copy and images before publication to confirm they accurately represent the vehicle, its features, its price, and its availability. For DigitalCLIQ work this means AI imagery is never presented as a specific VIN (especially used units, FAQ Q11), and AI-drafted price or payment copy is checked against the live feed before it ships.
rules.fail_condition: Not website-verifiable. Advisory for every report and a hard gate inside DigitalCLIQ's own creative skills: no AI-generated image or copy ships as a representation of a specific vehicle, price, or availability without a human check against the feed
rules.source: FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection staff remarks (Michael Dingman, Assistant Director, NAMVBC, 2026-09-30; his own views, not the Commission's), summarized by ComplyAuto (Hao Nguyen, 2026-10-05), https://complyauto.com/ftc-consumer-protection-official-shares-perspective-on-pricing-transparency-for-dealers/

cars_act_reference.dmv_disclaimer: DMV states its page is only a summary and that enforcement follows the exact text of the Vehicle Code and Civil Code. Where the summary and the chaptered statute differ, the statute controls.
cars_act_reference.applies_to: Licensed California dealers selling or leasing light-duty vehicles (GVWR under 10,000 lb), new and used.
exemptions_per_dmv: fleet sales (DMV summary says five or more units)
commercial purchasers buying five or more vehicles per year
exemptions_per_statute: wholesale sales (not a retail sale under Rev. & Tax. Code 6007)
vehicles not required to be registered
fleet sales: MORE THAN ONE vehicle in a single transaction, primarily for business or commercial use (Civ. Code 1784.31(f)(2))
commercial purchasers: five or more vehicles from that dealer per year, primarily for business use
vehicles with GVWR of 10,000 lb or more
known_discrepancies: Fleet threshold: DMV summary says five or more units; chaptered text says more than one vehicle in a single transaction. Apply the statute. Flagged for counsel and for the next legal-watch pass.
Used-vehicle cancellation: DMV says vehicles 'valued' $50,000 or less; statute keys on purchase or lease price. Apply the statute.
Mileage: DMV says 'around 400 miles'; statute says the right is lost if the vehicle is driven more than 400 miles. Apply the statute.
cars_act_reference.first_communication_rule_dmv_wording: Total price must appear in the first email, text, document, or form mentioning the vehicle or financing. Ads must be clear and conspicuous.
cars_act_reference.cooling_off_dmv_wording: Three days including weekends, for any reason, used vehicles $50,000 or less; mileage limit and restocking fee of $200 to $600 may apply.
cars_act_reference.records_dmv_wording: Retain for two years: advertisements, first communications, pricing disclosures, add-on consents, cancellation notices.
cars_act_reference.federal_posture_dmv_wording: Mirrors many provisions of the federal CARS Rule but is enforceable at the state level following federal disapproval.

consumer_complaint_channels.channel: Record of Complaint form, online, or by phone

biggest_risks_first_120_days: Installed or effectively required add-on products left out of the total price (highest-dollar, actively pursued by regulators)
First-written-communication failures in the BDC and CRM: auto-replies, templates, salesperson texts that reference a vehicle without the price

Three-day cancellation mechanics: wrong form, miscounted period, mishandled refund or trade-in
cncda_guidance.advertisement_definition: Any statement the dealer intentionally communicates to the public generally to promote a sale (13 CCR 255.00(b)): website listings, dealer-fed third-party listings, dealer-authored stickers, mailers, email blasts, social posts including employee personal accounts.
cncda_guidance.advertised_price_is_a_ceiling: Veh. Code 11713.1(e): sell at or below the advertised total price to any person while unsold, whether or not the buyer saw the ad, unless the ad stated an expiration that has passed. Date every price ad and every CRM/BDC template.
cncda_guidance.plus_disclosure_verbatim: Plus government fees and taxes, any finance charges, any dealer document processing charge, any electronic filing charge, and any emission testing charge.
cncda_guidance.federal_dpc_posture: FTC staff stated in April 2026 (NADA webinar) that the most prominent advertised price must include every dealer-imposed mandatory charge including the document processing charge; written FTC guidance had not issued as of 2026-08-07 and dealer associations are seeking it. California law keeps the DPC, electronic filing charge, and emission testing charge outside total price. CNCDA's optional dual-compliant format: 'Total Price', 'Document processing charge (not a governmental fee)', 'Price including document processing charge', DPC-inclusive figure at least equal prominence, taxes and government fees still excluded, never labeled out-the-door.

first_written_communication.trigger: Content and context, not channel. Email, text, chat, digital-retailing message, or a worksheet shown to a walk-in all qualify; a verbal quote does not. A reply to a vehicle-specific inquiry is a response regarding that vehicle whether or not it names the vehicle.
auto_reply_configurations: Merge the vehicle's total price from inventory into the auto-reply
Bare administrative receipt only (no vehicle reference, no marketing, no credit invitation), then the first substantive reply states the total price
first_written_communication.text_opt_in: Consent mechanics only; no vehicle reference, price, or promotion. First substantive text after consent carries the total price.
first_written_communication.ai_agent: Next substantive reply after a specific vehicle is named states the total price; a bare transfer notice may precede it but the price follows promptly.
first_written_communication.link_only: Not recommended. State the total price in the message body; a link is supplemental. Counsel before adopting a link-in-place-of-price process.
first_written_communication.credit_only_inquiry: No trigger. Avoid quoting rates, payments, or amounts until a vehicle is identified.
first_written_communication.walk_in: First worksheet, printed quote, or electronic message that references the vehicle. Reynolds Total Price Disclosure form LAWCA-TOTPRCDISC adds a signature; no signature is required by the Act, the disclosure must be made, not acknowledged.
first_written_communication.personal_phones: Only through a dealership-managed app routed to the CRM or a retained platform; written policy; Labor Code 2802 reimbursement applies.
first_written_communication.safest_bdc_reply: State the total price and nothing more; reserve payment figures for desked terms.

reynolds_forms.LAWCA-TOTPRCDISC: Total Price Disclosure (any deal, keyed to advertising and first communication)
reynolds_forms.LAWCA-PCD 10/26: Pre-Contract Disclosure for retail installment sale contracts; must match the contract exactly; lower-payment notice preprinted
reynolds_forms.LAWCA-OPD: Optional Add-On Products or Services Disclosure; lease and cash deals, and finance deals with add-ons outside the PCD categories; disclose at first written presentation, document at signing
reynolds_forms.LAWCA-CANCELDSCL: 3-Day Right to Cancel Used Car Purchase or Lease disclosure, every covered used deal
reynolds_forms.LAWCA-CANCELACKN: Acknowledgment of Cancellation and Receipt (itemized unwind)
reynolds_forms.LAWCA-CANCELFAIL: Notice of Failure to Meet Cancellation Requirement(s); not statutory, protective only when grounds are accurate; manager signs
reynolds_forms.553CA1026: Reynolds Retail Installment Sale Contract carrying the first-page cancellation language
reynolds_forms.order: Reynolds Document Service Consultant, CelinaCustomerService@reyrey.com, 1.800.344.0996; eForms through the DMS provider

three_day_mechanics.clock: Runs from execution of the agreement, not delivery; three calendar days starting the day after execution, ending at posted close of business, extended to the next open day if day three falls on a closed day (holidays included). 400 miles measured from execution.
three_day_mechanics.threshold: $50,000 inclusive on purchase price or capitalized cost; CNCDA recommends granting the right whenever the vehicle price is at or under $50,000 even if optional add-ons push the amount financed higher.
three_day_mechanics.restocking_fee: 1.5% of sale price, $200 floor, $600 cap (or actual shipping cost up to that cap), plus $1 per mile over 250 capped at $150. Deducted from the refund first; only a shortfall is due at the door.
three_day_mechanics.refund: Within 48 hours of exercise; two business days after verification for non-verified payment methods, with documentation; unverified funds never justify rejecting the cancellation. Refund tax attributable to refunded amounts and claim with CDTFA; registration fees are not a deduction.
three_day_mechanics.trade_in: Return it if unsold; otherwise the greatest of contract allowance, gross resale price (reconditioning not deducted), or fair market value supported by a 7-day written offer or a pricing-guide printout, less only indebtedness actually paid; redacted proof of sale if the store says it sold the trade. Consider holding trades for the window.
three_day_mechanics.rollback: A three-day return is a DMV rollback, not an unwind: report of sale stands, DMV fees are not refunded to the dealer, document with bill of sale, REG 262, REG 256; notify the lender and cancel the assignment.
three_day_mechanics.signage: 36-point physical notice in each sales office and cubicle where written terms are discussed and each contract room; may share a poster if the text stays 36-point; Reynolds supplies it.

cncda_guidance.records_practical: Retain the DMS or inventory-provider feed export by vehicle and date with the vendor's written confirmation of two-year retrievability; dated site and third-party captures supplement it. Keep creative with run dates and placement only where it states a total price or payment for a specific vehicle; mailers with mailing date and list identifiers. Export the full two-year CRM history before any migration. Complaints exclude surveys, reviews, testimonials. CNCDA advises against over-retention.
cncda_guidance.enforcement: No express private right of action; DMV has no direct authority; expect UCL, FAL, and CLRA suits, AG and DA actions, DMV Vehicle Code theories, and FTC Section 5. SB 478 hidden-fee law: only Veh. Code 11713.1(b) fees may be excluded from an advertised price under the dealer safe harbor.

resolved_open_questions.lease_advertising: Covered in practice when a specific unit is identified; MSRP used to identify a class does not trigger it (FAQ Q19)
resolved_open_questions.class_ads: No identified unit means no total-price trigger; 'starting at' quantity and VIN rules still apply (Guide Appendix D Ex. 6)
resolved_open_questions.optional_installed_items: Must be priced in; pay-or-remove is unlawful; dealer need not remove or discount a refused item (Guide Part 2, FAQ Q48)
resolved_open_questions.internet_tool_carve_out: Plainly covers the lower-payment comparison notice; total-of-payments coverage is arguable; configure tools to show both (FAQ Q40)
resolved_open_questions.used_lease_threshold: Purchase price or capitalized cost of $50,000 or less (FAQ Section E)
resolved_open_questions.private_right_of_action: None express; UCL, FAL, CLRA vehicles expected (Guide Part 8)
resolved_open_questions.section_1632_languages: Spanish, Chinese, Tagalog, Vietnamese, Korean (Guide Part 3)
resolved_open_questions.delay: No delaying or amending legislation enacted or pending as of 2026-08-31 (FAQ Q69)

faq_digest.Q1: Why price transparency: the advertised price must be the price the consumer will actually pay, aside from required government charges such as taxes.
faq_digest.Q2: Advertised price = the actual price any consumer can walk in and pay. Exclude only amounts a federal, state, or local agency requires the CONSUMER to pay directly. Everything else is in, including dealer fees a government authorizes but does not mandate, and charges the government imposes on the dealer that the dealer passes on.
faq_digest.Q3: Every medium: dealer and third-party websites, social media, print, roadside signs, and phone calls and text messages with dealer staff. A price stated anywhere must be truthful and transparent.
faq_digest.Q4: Any webpage stating any amount a consumer may pay, including inventory-search pages and vehicle-listing pages, must show the actual price as the most prominent amount.
faq_digest.Q5: MSRP, discounts, and rebates may appear if the actual price is the most prominent amount. Prominence is not only font size: a smaller MSRP placed where it draws the eye defeats prominence, and labels like 'the price you'll get' near both numbers are confusing. A conditional discount (first responders, dealer financing) may be offered if the price any consumer pays, with any financing, is most prominent and the terms are clear.
faq_digest.Q6: Document fee: the advertised price must include the full mandatory doc fee. FTC's example: $40,000 vehicle plus $85 doc fee must be advertised at $40,085. If some buyers are charged a higher mandatory fee than others, the advertised price must carry the highest.
faq_digest.Q7: State doc-fee rules (separate disclosure, caps, wording) are additive. First make the all-in price the most prominent amount, then add whatever state disclosures are required.
faq_digest.Q8: Leases: processing fees due upfront must be included in any advertised total amount due upfront. Reg M, Reg Z, and other federal duties are unchanged.
faq_digest.Q9: Negotiation and optional items: the advertised price cannot rest on a discount or negotiated price only some buyers got. Dealers may not suggest an optional add-on is required, imply an installed option cannot be removed and must be paid for, misstate an option's cost, or charge for options the consumer did not agree to.
faq_digest.Q10: Vehicles not on the lot (in transit, offsite, inventory sharing) may be advertised only if the ad plainly says the car is not on the lot. In-transit units must actually be in transit and not allocated to another consumer's paid order. Sold, delivered, or unavailable units may not be advertised to draw traffic and steer buyers up.
faq_digest.Q11: Representative photos only when the pictured car is the same make, model, condition, and other material characteristics and a reasonable consumer understands it is illustrative. Common for new and in-transit units; for used and antique cars consumers expect the photo to be the exact car.
faq_digest.Q12: Shared responsibility: dealers give third parties the actual price, take all steps in their control to make it most prominent, and avoid contradictory internal instructions; third-party advertisers show it most prominently; OEM policies must not conflict. Dealers remain responsible for every ad under their name.
faq_digest.Q13: No grace period: Section 5 price transparency has applied for decades.
faq_digest.Q14: Report violations, including competitors, at ReportFraud.ftc.gov with ad copies or contracts.

open_questions_resolved.document_processing_charge: Answered: must be inside the most prominent advertised price (Q6), and state doc-fee disclosure rules are additive (Q7).
open_questions_resolved.electronic_filing_and_emission_testing_c: Answered by Q2 in principle and BY NAME in the 2026-09-30 staff remarks: if the government does not require the consumer to pay the charge but the dealer does, it belongs in the advertised price; the label does not resolve it, the underlying legal obligation does; the dealer may absorb the cost instead of charging it. ComplyAuto state-by-state analysis still pending.
open_questions_resolved.either_or_oem_incentives: Largely answered by the Q5 dealer-financing example: a finance-conditioned discount may be advertised alongside the price, but the most prominent price must be the one a buyer using any financing pays.
open_questions_resolved.as_low_as_and_subset_pricing: Not addressed by name; Q9 bars an advertised price based on a discount only some buyers get, and Q5 requires the all-comers price be most prominent.
open_questions_resolved.no_price_listings: Not addressed by the FAQs. 2026-09-30 staff remarks: 'Get My Price' or 'Call for Price' buttons may appear ALONGSIDE the advertised price if they do not imply a lower price or obscure the real one (FTC-CTA-001). California separately bars call-for-price and price-gating CTAs from 2026-10-01 (CA-CARS-026).
open_questions_resolved.in_production_units: Answered in substance by the 2026-09-30 staff remarks: consumers read 'in transit' as already on its way, so a unit not yet built or shipped must be described by its actual status, never as in transit (FTC-AVAIL-003). Stated arrival dates must reflect what the dealer knows.

california_tension.summary: California Veh. Code §11713.1 and the CARS Act total-price definition keep the document processing charge (capped), electronic filing charge, and emission testing charge outside the advertised total price, and the CA Plus Disclosure names them as extra. FTC Q2, Q6, and Q7 say dealer-imposed and passed-through charges belong inside the most prominent price regardless of state doc-fee rules.
california_tension.cncda_format_before_faq: CNCDA Guide v1.2 dual format: Total Price, then 'Document processing charge (not a governmental fee)', then 'Price including document processing charge', with the DPC-inclusive figure at least as prominent as total price, never labeled out-the-door.
california_tension.interpretive_posture: INTERPRETIVE, confirm with counsel and the next CNCDA update. The FAQ asks that the all-in figure be THE most prominent amount, not merely equal. Conservative presentation for California stores: make the price including the document processing charge (and any electronic filing or emission charge the dealer passes on) the single most prominent figure, show the CARS Act total price and the Plus Disclosure less prominently beneath it, and never label either figure out-the-door. Skill findings on this point ship as warnings with human review, not criticals, while the state and federal positions are reconciled.
california_tension.update_2026_10_08: The 2026-09-30 staff remarks name the electronic filing and emission testing charges: under the federal test they belong in the price when the dealer requires them. The conservative California layout now covers all three Plus Disclosure extras: price including the document processing charge, electronic filing charge, and emission testing charge as the single most prominent figure; CARS Act total price and the verbatim Plus Disclosure beneath it; neither labeled out-the-door. Still a warning with human review until CNCDA responds.

staff_remarks_2026_09_30.binding_status: Assistant Director's own views, not the Commission's or any Commissioner's; they do not amend the FAQs. Best available read of how FTC staff will apply Section 5 to the scenarios the FAQs left open. Treat as INTERPRETIVE.

digest.government_fee_test: Excludable only when the consumer is legally obligated to pay the charge to the government (taxes, consumer-owed title and registration). A state law authorizing or capping a doc fee does not make it governmental. A government fee imposed on the dealer and passed through is in the price. Emission testing and electronic filing charges: same test, by name; the dealer may absorb them.
digest.itemization: Breakdowns of MSRP, rebates, discounts, and included fees are allowed once the most prominent price is the any-consumer price. A fee name must not imply a benefit not provided; state fee-identification rules apply.
digest.optional_add_ons: Optional must be real: the customer can decline and buy at the advertised price. A mandatory add-on is in the price. No charging for products not agreed to; costs accurately described.
digest.savings_claims: Judged in context. 'Save $10,000' may not imply inventory-wide savings when it is one unit or trim. Financing or trade-in conditions must be clear. Disclosing a condition does not let a subset-only price be the most prominent price.
digest.cta_buttons: 'Get My Price' / 'Call for Price' may sit alongside the advertised price. Must not suggest a lower price is available if untrue, and must not obscure or contradict the advertised price.
digest.in_transit: 'In transit' means already on its way. Not yet built or shipped: describe that status instead. In-transit units must be available on arrival and not allocated to another paid order.
digest.delivery_timelines: The Commission has previously pointed to delivery within one to two business days. Delays outside the dealer's control are judged case by case (routine vs isolated); stated arrival dates must match what the dealer knows.
digest.third_party_control: Each party controlling an ad can be responsible (dealer, OEM, vendor, listing site). Report OEM policies or platform limitations that block compliant display to ReportFraud.ftc.gov with documentation.
digest.cloned_websites: Report impersonating sites to ReportFraud@ftc.gov with the URL and what was copied.
digest.ai_in_advertising: AI does not change the obligation. Review AI-generated copy and images before publication for accuracy on vehicle, features, price, and availability.
